candidates.evidence: Spectrum shows five sample modes at 123.8, 240.4, 263.5, 368.7 and 550.7 cm-1 plus Si, the general pattern expected for a metal thiophosphate (MPS3-type). Positions do not match my recollection of FePS3 bands: 550.7 cm-1 is ~25 cm-1 below the ~575 cm-1 band I recall, and 263.5 and 368.7 are ~10-20 cm-1 below the ~280 and ~380 cm-1 bands I recall. Literature values are unverified here (no reference data or internet access).

hint_reasoning: The spectrum has the broad character of an MPS3-type metal thiophosphate: a few sharp modes in 100-600 cm-1, with the strongest at 368.7 cm-1 and a second strong band at 263.5 cm-1. It does not clearly match FePS3 as I recall the room-temperature 532 nm literature. The most diagnostic mismatch is the highest-frequency P2S6-unit band, which I recall near 575 cm-1 for FePS3 but which appears at 550.7 cm-1 here; that is about 25 cm-1 off, far more than the Si calibration offset (+0.17 cm-1) or the expected few-cm-1 temperature shift between 295 K and low-temperature literature. The 263.5 and 368.7 bands are also 10-20 cm-1 below my recalled values. Because my reference values are recalled rather than checked, this is an inconsistency at low-to-moderate confidence, not a proof that the sample is a different material. The absence of a resolved magnetic feature is consistent with 295 K being above T_N (~118 K) but does not discriminate. A reference FePS3 spectrum at the same temperature and laser would settle the question.

limits: No FePS3 reference spectrum or internet access was available, so the FePS3 band positions are from memory and need checking against the cited paper or an in-house reference at 295 K and 532 nm. The verdict rests on those recalled values.
The spectrum is a single unpolarised measurement with no angle series, so polarization classification (isotropic/twofold/fourfold) does not apply and no symmetry (irrep) assignments are made.
Band assignments are unknown: the data do not identify which mode of FePS3 each peak is, so they cannot separately confirm the material from mode symmetry.
Noise is about 560 counts per point, against sample band heights of 2000-10500 counts. Weak modes under about 2000 counts could be missed. The 74.7 cm-1 component is marginal and tentative.
Peak positions are raw fitted values. The Si line sits 0.17 cm-1 above 520.7 cm-1, so a calibration correction would shift all positions by about -0.2 cm-1; this does not change the conclusions.

A broad background of about 2500-3500 counts (fluorescence or substrate contribution) was removed with a low-order polynomial baseline. Baseline order 4-10 gave stable positions to within 0.1 cm-1 and widths to within about 1 cm-1 for the stronger bands.
No single-point cosmic-ray spikes were found. The narrow 520-521 cm-1 pair is the Si substrate line, confirmed by its position and width.

The working-directory name contains the string 'CdPS3'. This was not used as evidence in the analysis; it is noted only because it conflicts with the stated FePS3 hint and would be a labelling issue to check if the sample identity is uncertain.
Magnetic (two-magnon or spin-phonon) features are not expected at 295 K above T_N, so their absence does not discriminate between candidate materials.
